The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration INSERT interpolates raw host strings into SQL, allowing SQL injection or crashes on values containing quotes

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration loops over `records.each do |h|` (from `site_settings.value` for `embeddable_hosts`) and runs:

```ruby
execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
```

`h` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL string with no escaping/parameterization. If any stored host value contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the migration can break (syntax error) and can potentially allow SQL injection within the migration context. This is a concrete defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update fetches and re-serializes an OpenStruct without reading params or saving, making it a silent no-op that reports success

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without reading any `params` or persisting anything. `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`), so a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` will return a successful serialized response but cannot apply any updates. This is a verifiable no-op update action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController raises NoMethodError (500) instead of 404/422 when given a nonexistent id for destroy or update
Plural hydration in store.js.es6 can leave false/undefined entries in the hydrated array when a side-loaded record lookup fails, unlike the guarded singular branch

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `store.js.es6` the new plural hydration branch does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns it directly: `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Unlike the singular branch (which only sets `obj[subType]` if `hydrated` is truthy), the plural branch does not filter or guard failed lookups. If `_lookupSubType` returns `null`/`undefined` for any id, the resulting array will contain those falsey entries, leaving `undefined`/`null` elements in the hydrated association array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricators are defined in swapped files: category_fabricator.rb defines embeddable_host and vice versa
deleteHost action's destroyRecord().then() has no .catch, so a failed DELETE leaves the row with no error shown to the admin

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); }); with no .catch handler. If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and no popupAjaxError (or other feedback) is shown; the row also won’t be removed because deleteHost is only sent in the success callback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757_interpolates host strings unescaped directly into raw INSERT SQL, breaking on quotes and creating a SQL injection vector via the setting value

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the existing site setting value (`val = embeddable_hosts[0]['value']`), splits it into `h`, and then executes raw SQL with direct string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. Because `h` is not quoted/escaped via the connection adapter, a host value containing a single-quote will break the SQL, and a crafted value could inject additional SQL. This is a verifiable correctness/security problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757 doesn't safely commit site setting deletion if the insert fails mid-way

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration performs inserts into `embeddable_hosts` and then executes `DELETE FROM site_settings ...` at the end. In Rails, migrations are run inside a single database transaction by default (unless `disable_ddl_transaction!` is used, which it is not here). Therefore, if any insert fails mid-way and raises an exception, the entire migration (including the final deletion) is rolled back and will not be committed. The finding claims the deletion could be committed even if inserts fail, but that is not verifiable from this diff under normal Rails transactional migration behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757 crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id queries return zero rows (e.g. fresh installs)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`: it does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` and later `execute(...)[0]['value'].to_i` without checking that the SQL result has any rows. If either query returns zero rows (e.g., no `site_settings` row for `embed_category` or `uncategorized_category_id`, or the join finds no matching category), `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']`/`nil['value']` raises `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration before the `category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host runs lower(host) = ? query on every embedded-comments request with no supporting index or caching, and lower() prevents use of a plain index on host

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, `record_for_host` performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` and `host_allowed?` is called from both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, i.e., on embed-related requests. The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates the `embeddable_hosts` table but does not add any index on `host`, and the query applies `lower()` to the column, which would also prevent use of a plain btree index on `host` even if one were added later (without a functional index or different query). This is a verifiable performance issue introduced by the diff (no caching and no supporting index).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op but fetch_embedding before_filter still eagerly loads and serializes all EmbeddableHost records on every update call

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `before_filter :fetch_embedding` runs for both `show` and `update`. `fetch_embedding` builds `@embedding` with `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`, which issues a query loading all EmbeddableHost records. The `update` action itself does not persist any changes (it just re-renders the serializer), so calling `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` will still eagerly load and serialize all hosts even though nothing is updated. This is directly verifiable from the diff and represents unnecessary work on every update call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddingController materializes all embeddable hosts with no pagination or limit

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding`, the model includes `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`, which does indeed load all embeddable hosts without pagination or an explicit limit. However, the diff does not establish any requirement or expectation for pagination/limits here, and this is an admin-only configuration screen where showing the full list is a reasonable design choice. As written, it’s a scalability/performance concern only under unusually large datasets, not a clear defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded maps every *_ids key unconditionally, producing arrays of undefined entries when a sub-type isn't found instead of skipping

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded` now matches `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and, for keys ending in `_ids`, it does `obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and assigns the result directly to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, then **always** deletes `obj[k]`. Unlike the singular `_id` case (which only sets `obj[subType]` and deletes the key if `hydrated` is truthy), the plural branch does not filter out missing lookups. If `_lookupSubType` returns `null/undefined` for an ID not found in `root`, the resulting array will contain `undefined` entries, and the original ids list is discarded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update passes a possibly-nil host into save_host without find/404, causing a 500 error on bad id

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If no record exists for the given `:id`, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...`, which will raise a `NoMethodError` and result in a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.rb expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host exists

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, but that setting is also removed from `site_settings.yml` and the host-allowlist logic is migrated to the `EmbeddableHost` model/table (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`). `expandable_first_post?` still gates on `has_topic_embed?`, so it only affects topics that already have a `TopicEmbed`. With the old setting gone, the removed check isn’t a verifiable defect by itself; it’s consistent with the refactor and there’s no clear correctness/security bug demonstrated in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings (from `config/site_settings.yml` and server locale docs) and deletes `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`, but it also adds a database-backed replacement (`EmbeddableHost`) and includes a migration that copies existing `site_settings` values into `embeddable_hosts` and then deletes the old settings. Whether this needs a “deprecation path” for “public external API consumers” is not a verifiable defect from the diff itself; it’s an intentional internal configuration change with an explicit data migration, and the claim about external API breakage is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController#update/#destroy raise unhandled 500 on unknown id because nil host is not handled

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then calls `save_host(host)`. If no record exists, `host` is `nil` and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` (500). Similarly, `#destroy` fetches with `.first` and then calls `host.destroy` without a nil check, also raising `NoMethodError` on unknown IDs. No 404/handled error path is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded plural-id handling breaks on nil/empty entries, non-array values, and irregular plurals, crashing hydration
Error message drift on embed endpoint: distinct 'embeddable hosts not set' error collapsed into generic 'invalid referer host' message

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the explicit `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set') if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` and replaces the check with `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. If there are zero allowed hosts, `host_allowed?` returns false and the error raised becomes `'invalid referer host'`. However, this is an intentional behavior/message change rather than a clear defect: the endpoint still correctly denies access when no hosts are configured, and no tests or code in the diff rely on the old specific error message. This is “message drift”, but not a verifiable bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update accepts and ignores any payload, returning success without saving anything

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `def update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads `params` or persists anything (and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`). The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` exposes this endpoint, and the client calls `embedding.update({})`, but any payload would be ignored and the response indicates success without saving changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update crashes with 500 when embeddable_host wrapper param is missing

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, the code blindly dereferences nested params: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If the `embeddable_host` wrapper key is missing (or nil), this will raise a `NoMethodError` (`undefined method [] for nil:NilClass`) and result in a 500. There is no guard (e.g., `params.require(:embeddable_host)`) or error handling in create/update to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with nil deref when embed_category setting is absent, since execute(...)[0]['id'] assumes a row exists (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11-12)

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute("... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If there is no `site_settings` row for `embed_category` (common if the setting was never explicitly saved, since defaults can come from YAML), `execute(...)` returns an empty result and `[0]` is nil, so `nil['id']` raises. The later `if category_id == 0` fallback won’t run because the exception occurs first.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection / migration failure from unescaped host setting values interpolated directly into INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts SQL (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:29-30)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration reads legacy `site_settings.value` for `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into `h`, and then does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. Because `h` is interpolated directly into SQL without quoting/escaping, any host value containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will break the migration and could potentially execute unintended SQL. Even if the setting is typically admin-controlled, it’s still untrusted persisted data at migration time and should be inserted via `quote`/binds rather than string interpolation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrated hosts copied verbatim with http:// or https:// prefixes never match uri.host in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, silently breaking embedding after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` copies the old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` entries directly into the new `embeddable_hosts.host` column via raw SQL `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, which bypasses the model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the stored value is `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (which the old setting logic/tests explicitly allowed), it will not equal `discourse.org`/`example.com`, so `host_allowed?` will return false and embedding will fail after upgrade for those migrated rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that never reads params or persists anything, causing silent data loss while showing success

adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is implemented as:
```rb
def update
  render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, root: 'embedding', rest_serializer: true)
end
```
It never reads `params` and never writes to any model or setting, yet the route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` is added and the client controller defines `saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }`, which will issue a PUT expecting changes to be applied. As written, the endpoint will always respond with a successful serialized payload without persisting anything, i.e., a silent no-op update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update and destroy crash with NoMethodError on nil host for stale ids, yielding 500s instead of clean errors
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController can crash with a NoMethodError when the host lookup returns nil (e.g., stale/nonexistent IDs), matching the golden issue about missing nil-check/validation after querying by id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost#host nil crashes before_validation with NoMethodError, rendering 500 instead of validation error path
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: the before_validation callback calls a mutating string method on `self.host`, and when `host` is nil it raises a NoMethodError (leading to a 500 instead of a validation failure).

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroyRecord().then() in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch, leaving unhandled promise rejection and no user feedback on delete failure

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... }); without any rejection handler. If the DELETE request fails, the returned promise will reject with no .catch (unlike the save() action which does .catch(popupAjaxError)), resulting in an unhandled rejection and no user-visible error feedback for delete failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host doesn't validate category_id references an existing category, allowing dangling category_id and broken UI rendering

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, `host.category_id` is taken directly from `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (or set to uncategorized if blank) and then `host.save` is called with no check that the category exists. The EmbeddableHost model only has `belongs_to :category` and a host format validation; there is no `validates :category, presence: true` / inclusion check, and the migration does not add a foreign key constraint. This allows saving a record with a dangling `category_id`. On the client, the component’s `edit()` action does `this.get('host.category.id')`, which will throw if `host.category` can’t be hydrated (nil because the category doesn’t exist), causing broken UI behavior for that row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store _hydrateEmbedded plural branch doesn't filter undefined results from _lookupSubType, and pluralize(subType) may not match serializer naming for irregulars

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `_hydrateEmbedded` method, the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/`) maps each id via `_lookupSubType` and assigns the resulting array directly to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, then deletes the original `*_ids` key. Unlike the singular case (which only assigns/deletes when `hydrated` is truthy), the plural case does not check/filter falsy/undefined results from `_lookupSubType`, so missing embedded records would yield arrays containing `undefined` (and it also drops the original ids). This is a concrete behavioral inconsistency introduced by the diff. The additional claim about `pluralize(subType)` mismatching serializer naming for irregular plurals is speculative and not evidenced by the diff, but the undefined-results issue is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin controller specs only assert inheritance rather than exercising create, update, destroy, the category_id fallback, and validation error rendering

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add two new controller specs (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) that only assert the controller subclasses `Admin::AdminController` and do not exercise actions like `create/update/destroy` or edge cases like `category_id` fallback and error rendering. However, this is a test coverage critique rather than a concrete bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff; the application code could still be correct even with minimal specs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update never actually updates anything, it just re-renders the serialized record, and this bug ships untested

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` indeed does not persist any changes; it just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (id + `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). However, the actual editable data in this feature (allowed hosts + category) is saved through `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`create/update/destroy`), and the Ember component `embeddable-host` calls `host.save(props)` / `destroyRecord()` on the `embeddable-host` model. There’s no evidence in the diff that `embedding#update` is supposed to modify anything (no settings/fields are being updated, and the template doesn’t even invoke `saveChanges`). So while the method is a no-op and lightly tested, calling it a “bug” is not a strictly verifiable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host on update will raise NoMethodError when no record matches params[:id] (nil.host = ...)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If no record matches the given `params[:id]`, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on nil. There is no nil-check or 404 handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test asserts the newly-possible case for expandable_first_post? where no EmbeddableHost records exist but the method returns true; the retained test passes only vacuously and can't distinguish old from new behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` after moving the allowlist from a site setting to the `EmbeddableHost` table. That makes the method independent of whether any hosts are currently configured, but that is not clearly incorrect: the method is about whether a topic with an existing embed should be expandable/truncated, and embedded topics can still exist even if the allowlist is later emptied. The proposed finding is primarily about test coverage (and claims the behavior is problematic) rather than identifying a definite bug introduced by the diff, and the diff excerpt doesn’t conclusively show the absence/presence of relevant tests. As stated, it’s not a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration data-migration logic in create_embeddable_hosts is completely untested, including cases of settings never set, hosts with http:// prefixes, and embed_category pointing at a deleted category
Migration uses hand-rolled SQL with string interpolation and subselects that can raise ([0]['id'] on empty result), with a cmd_tuples > 0 check, untested

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute("SELECT ...")[0]['id'].to_i`. If that SELECT returns zero rows (e.g., no `site_settings` row matching embed_category / value mismatch), `execute(...)[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` will raise, aborting the migration. Additionally, it later builds an INSERT with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` where `h` comes from the existing `embeddable_hosts` setting; unescaped quotes or unexpected content can break the SQL (and is avoidable by parameterization/sanitization). These are concrete correctness risks present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host / host_allowed? have no direct tests for failure modes: malformed URLs, URLs with no host, or nil referer

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces EmbeddableHost.record_for_host and .host_allowed? with explicit failure handling (URI parse rescue, missing uri/host) but the added spec (spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb) only tests trimming and a couple of positive/negative host matches. There are no direct tests covering malformed URLs, URLs with no host, or nil input/referer-like cases for these methods. So the finding is factually verifiable as a test coverage gap in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded pluralization change lacks tests for empty xyz_ids: [] array, a model with both x_id and x_ids, and _lookupSubType returning false/undefined inside the map (resulting array will contain false values and hydrated || [] never kicks in)
Test for find('fruit', 2) actually receives fruits[0] (apple) from the pretender — the fixture identity isn't tied to the id, so it verifies the mock, not the requested record

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding refers to a test involving `find('fruit', 2)`, a Pretender mock, and a `fruits` fixture returning `fruits[0]` (apple). None of these concepts or code patterns appear anywhere in the provided diff (which adds embedding/embeddable host admin UI, adapters, Rails controllers/models/serializers, and related specs). Therefore the finding does not describe a verifiable issue introduced or present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Entire new admin embedding frontend (adapter, controller, stateful component with save/cancel/delete/rollback, pathFor override, and type.replace('_', '-') change in rest.js affecting all admin models) has no JS tests; route map and nav additions also untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new admin embedding frontend (adapter/component/controller/route/templates) and modifies the REST adapter behavior, but it does not add any JavaScript test files alongside these changes. However, the proposed finding is essentially about missing test coverage rather than a specific correctness/security bug introduced by the diff. Absence of JS tests is verifiable, but it is not a concrete defect in the implementation itself, and the diff does include some new Ruby specs for related controllers/models.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files are swapped in content: category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines :category fabricators — works by accident of file loading order and is a maintenance hazard suggesting accidental file rename/move
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have their fabricator definitions swapped (category file defines embeddable_host and vice versa), matching the golden issue about swapped contents leading to loss/misuse of the intended fabricators.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec only covers the happy path; no test for EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) returning false during import, where the category silently becomes nil instead of coming from SiteSetting.embed_category

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally removes the global `SiteSetting.embed_category` setting (deleted from `site_settings.yml`, locale text removed, and migration deletes it), and `TopicEmbed.import` now derives the category from the matching `EmbeddableHost` record (`eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` then `category: eh.try(:category_id)`). In the normal embed flow, invalid hosts are rejected before import (`TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now both call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`), so `record_for_host(url)` returning false should not occur on the main path. The proposed finding is primarily about missing test coverage and also assumes a fallback to `SiteSetting.embed_category` that no longer exists, so it does not point to a clear defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files have swapped contents: category_fabricator.rb was deleted and replaced with embeddable_host fabricator content while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the old category fabricators, creating a maintainability trap

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines any `:category` fabricators and instead defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the previous `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. This is a verifiable swap/misnaming that creates a maintainability hazard and could break setups that require fabricators by filename (expecting category fabricators in `category_fabricator.rb`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection / broken SQL in migration: user-configured host strings are interpolated directly into INSERT statement without quoting/escaping
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying security flaw: building an SQL statement by directly interpolating host strings (e.g., "#{h}") without proper quoting/binding, which can lead to SQL injection and/or broken SQL. The candidate differs on where it occurs (migration vs controller), but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh installs when embed_category/uncategorized_category_id site setting rows are absent, causing NoMethodError on nil from execute result

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for `embed_category` and later `execute(...)[0]['value'].to_i` for `uncategorized_category_id` with no guard for an empty result set. On a fresh install, the `site_settings` table often contains no rows for defaults like `embed_category`/`uncategorized_category_id` (it typically only stores overrides), so `execute(...)[0]` can be `nil`, making `['id']`/`['value']` raise `NoMethodError`. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unique DB index on embeddable_hosts.host and host_allowed? performs unindexed full-table lower(host) = ? scan per request; should add unique index and normalize host to lowercase
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is about case-insensitive matching being broken because only lower(host) is applied on the DB side while the input parameter isn’t normalized, so mixed-case hosts may not match. The candidate explicitly recommends normalizing the host to lowercase, which addresses the same functional mismatch, even though it also adds extra concerns about indexing/performance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update does nothing — re-renders serializer without applying params, making it dead code

adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is implemented as:
```rb
def update
  render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, root: 'embedding', rest_serializer: true)
end
```
It does not read or apply any request params and does not persist any changes (it just re-renders the same OpenStruct created in `fetch_embedding`). Given it is wired to a PUT route (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`) and the Ember controller has an action calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`, this is a verifiable no-op “update” endpoint (i.e., dead/ineffective for updating state).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController#update crashes with nil: params[:id] lookup with .first can return nil causing NoMethodError; params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises if key missing; update/destroy don't 404 on missing records

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists for that id, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host(host)` will immediately call `host.host = ...`, raising `NoMethodError`. Similarly, `destroy` calls `host.destroy` and will also raise on `nil`. Additionally, `save_host` assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` is present and does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` / `[:category_id]`; if that key is missing, it will raise `NoMethodError` rather than returning a validation/400-style error. There is no handling to return a 404/appropriate error on missing records or missing params, so the finding describes real crash paths introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded deletes *_ids key unconditionally even when hydration fails/empty, losing original ids; `hydrated || []` fallback never triggers since hydrated is an array

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch for keys ending in `_ids` always does `delete obj[k]` after mapping, regardless of whether `_lookupSubType` returns anything. Unlike the singular `_id` case (which only deletes when `hydrated` is truthy), the plural `_ids` case will remove the original id list even if hydration produces `undefined` entries (or if the embedded records aren’t present in `root`). Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead code because `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy), so the fallback won’t trigger. This matches the proposed finding and is a correctness regression risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adapter pathFor() ignores its type/id arguments and basePath globally munges type names with type.replace('_','-'), duplicating knowledge with ADMIN_MODELS registry

adjudication.rationale:
The new `admin/adapters/embedding` adapter hardcodes `pathFor()` to `/admin/customize/embedding`. Even if the parent adapter calls `pathFor(type, id)`, JavaScript will ignore extra arguments, and this model is clearly treated as a singleton (`id: 'default'` and routes `GET/PUT customize/embedding` without an `:id`), so ignoring `type/id` is not a correctness bug.

The `basePath` change in `discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6` only normalizes the `type` string for the `ADMIN_MODELS` membership check (`type.replace('_','-')`), which is necessary to match model naming (`embeddable_host`/`site_customization`) to the registry entries (`embeddable-host`/`site-customization`). This is not “duplicating knowledge” in a way that causes a defect; it’s an implementation detail to make the lookup work.

So the finding describes a design preference, not a verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Component bypasses store/buffer pattern: reads buffered.host via getProperties unwrapping buffer and manually sets host.set('category', ...) after save instead of relying on server response hydration
Update route uses PUT to a singleton pseudo-model with id 'default' (OpenStruct) — premature/fake abstraction that should be reduced since update never mutates anything

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a singleton-ish `Admin::EmbeddingController` that builds an `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and defines an `update` action that does not persist anything (it just re-renders the same serialized object). However, in the shown UI the actual mutable data (`EmbeddableHost`) is saved via its own REST resource (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`), so the no-op PUT is not a correctness/security defect—it's at most an arguably unnecessary endpoint/abstraction. The finding is primarily architectural/opinionated rather than a verifiable bug introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead locale key admin.embedding.edit defined but never referenced in any template

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the client locale key `admin.embedding.edit: "edit"` in `config/locales/client.en.yml`, but none of the new/modified templates reference `admin.embedding.edit` (the templates use `admin.embedding.host`, `admin.embedding.category`, `admin.embedding.add_host`, etc., and the edit button is icon-only). So the key appears unused. However, this is just an unused/extra translation entry and does not create a functional bug or correctness defect in the introduced code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs only assert class ancestry, providing no behavioral coverage for create/update/destroy including nil-record paths

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the newly added controller specs `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each contain only a single example asserting the controller is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. They do not exercise any controller actions (`create`, `update`, `destroy`, `show`) or validate responses/side effects, and therefore provide no behavioral coverage (including cases where `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` in `update`/`destroy`). This is directly verifiable from the spec contents.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration is irreversible: DELETE FROM site_settings runs inside change, so rollback drops the table but never restores the deleted embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings rows, permanently destroying original configuration

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` defines `def change` but performs multiple raw `execute` statements, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. In Rails, `execute` calls inside `change` are not automatically reversible, so rolling back this migration will raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` (and there is no `down` method to restore the deleted rows). Thus, it is true that the migration is irreversible and provides no way to restore the original `site_settings` rows on rollback (even if the exact “drops the table but not the settings” sequence is not how Rails will behave; it will typically fail before dropping anything).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh/minimal installs: execute(...)[0]['id'] raises NoMethodError when no embed_category row exists, and the uncategorized_category_id fallback also assumes a row exists

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does:

```rb
category_id = execute("... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If that SELECT returns zero rows (which is plausible on fresh/minimal installs, especially since this diff removes the `embed_category` site setting from `config/site_settings.yml`), then `execute(...)[0]` will be `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration.

The fallback has the same structural issue:

```rb
category_id = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i
```

If that row is missing for any reason at this migration point, it will also crash the same way. The first crash (missing `embed_category`) is directly introduced/likely due to changes in this diff, making the finding a real, verifiable defect in the migration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill inserts hosts raw without normalization: protocol-prefixed hosts like https://example.com will never match example.com under the new lower(host) = uri.host comparison, silently breaking embedding after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` backfills by doing a raw SQL insert of each line from the old `site_settings` value: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` without any normalization. Existing settings could include `http://...`, `https://...`, or paths (the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly handled those cases). Under the new logic, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the stored row contains `https://example.com/1234`, it will never equal `example.com`, so embedding access checks (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`) will fail after upgrade. This mismatch is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL built by string interpolation in migration INSERT: host values from admin-entered settings may contain quotes, causing crashes or SQL injection; should use quote/parameterized insert

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The `h` value comes from the prior `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts` (admin-entered). If `h` contains a single quote or other SQL syntax, the INSERT can fail (syntax error) and could potentially allow SQL injection within the migration context. Proper quoting (e.g., `connection.quote(h)`) or parameterization is needed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true on create_table silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table, destroying data on environments where the table already exists

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists (typically via `DROP TABLE`), then recreate it. That would destroy any existing data in `embeddable_hosts` on environments where the table already exists for any reason, matching the finding’s claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill assumes embeddable_hosts setting is newline-delimited raw text, but host_list serialization (YAML/JSON in some versions) may cause split("\n") to produce one garbage row instead of N hosts

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the old `site_settings.value` for `embeddable_hosts` is fetched as a single string and split on `"\n"`. The diff shows `embeddable_hosts` was a `type: host_list` setting, which in Discourse is stored as newline-delimited text in the DB (a textarea-style list), not as YAML/JSON. The claim that it may be YAML/JSON-serialized “in some versions” is not supported or verifiable from this diff, so the finding is speculative rather than a concrete defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NOT NULL category_id with no default plus fragile non-atomic raw SQL lookup in migration: if uncategorized_category_id resolves to 0/invalid, backfilled host inserts fail against the constraint

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts.category_id` with `null: false` but then backfills with an integer `category_id` that can become `0` via `to_i`. However, `0` satisfies the NOT NULL constraint, so inserts will not fail “against the constraint” merely because the category id is invalid. There is no foreign key or check constraint shown in the diff that would reject `0`. While the SQL lookup/backfill is fragile in other ways (e.g., `execute(...)[0]['id']` can raise if the query returns no rows, and the INSERT uses unsafe string interpolation), the specific failure mode claimed (NOT NULL + no default causing backfill insert failure when id is 0/invalid) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing index on host for the hot lookup path: record_for_host runs lower(host) = ? on every embed request, causing a full table scan; lowercase comparison also defeats a plain index

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new `embeddable_hosts` table migration (`20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`) creates `host` but adds no index on it. Meanwhile `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` queries with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` and this is called on request paths like `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Without an index (and especially with `lower(host)`), this will typically result in a full table scan rather than an indexed lookup unless a functional index exists (none is created in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin controller crashes on unknown id: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first can be nil, causing NoMethodError in save_host(nil) and destroy raising on nil, producing a 500 instead of 404/422

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController, both update and destroy do `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without handling a missing record. If no record matches, `host` is nil. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...` which will raise NoMethodError on nil. `destroy` does `host.destroy` which will also raise NoMethodError. This would produce a 500 error instead of a 404/not_found or a validation-style error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update doesn't update anything — it just re-serializes, so any future embedding-level settings silently no-op

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController`, `update` indeed ignores params and simply re-renders `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`), so it performs no persistence. However, in this diff there are no embedding-level attributes/settings to update: `EmbeddingSerializer` only exposes `id` and `embeddable_hosts` (which are managed via the separate `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` CRUD). The client `saveChanges()` calls `embedding.update({})` with an empty object and there is no template/UI shown that relies on `update` to change anything. The claim about “future embedding-level settings silently no-op” is speculative beyond the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data-migration logic embedded in schema migration makes it impossible to roll back the schema without losing the data backfill, violating data/schema migration separation

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` mixes schema changes (`create_table :embeddable_hosts`) with data backfill and destructive data changes: it reads from `site_settings`, inserts rows into `embeddable_hosts`, and then executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. Because it uses a `change` method with raw `execute` statements (not reversible), a rollback would drop the new table but would not restore the deleted `site_settings` rows or undo the inserted data, making rollback lossy. This is exactly the “data migration embedded in schema migration / rollback can’t restore previous state” issue described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingAdapter pathFor() returns constant '/admin/customize/embedding' ignoring record id, so update/delete/create target the wrong route
No adapter for the 'embedding' model; store.find('embedding') requests /embeddings which has no route, breaking admin page load

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an Ember Data adapter for the `embedding` model at `app/assets/javascripts/admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6`. That adapter overrides `pathFor()` to return `"/admin/customize/embedding"`, which matches the new Rails routes (`get/put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#show/update"`). Therefore `this.store.find('embedding')` will not default to `/embeddings`; it will use this adapter path, so the admin page should load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update never reads params or persists anything, returning success while saving nothing

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and does not read `params` or persist any changes. It also uses `@embedding` built in `fetch_embedding` as an `OpenStruct` (not an ActiveRecord model), so there is nothing to save. Additionally, the client-side controller defines `saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }`, which would hit the PUT route and receive a successful response despite no server-side mutation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController crashes with NoMethodError when host record not found (nil) instead of returning 404

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the host is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists, `host` is `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)`, and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on nil. `destroy` calls `host.destroy` without a nil check, also raising `NoMethodError`. There is no `404`/not-found handling in either path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting row doesn't exist due to nil access on execute(...)[0]['id']
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same root cause as the golden comment: the migration assumes execute(...)[0]['id'] exists and will crash when the embed_category setting row is missing (no rows returned), due to nil access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL interpolation in migration INSERT with raw string values enables SQL injection and breaks on quotes

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes from the `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` (split by newlines). If `h` contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, the INSERT will break, and because it’s executed as raw SQL it also creates an injection risk (migration runs with full DB privileges and the setting could be attacker-controlled in some deployments). This is a real, verifiable issue in the diff; it should use proper quoting/bind parameters (e.g., `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or `insert` APIs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration deletes embeddable_hosts and embed_category settings unconditionally with no down method, risking data loss

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` ends with `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`, and it uses a `change` method with raw SQL, so it is not automatically reversible. However, in the context of this diff those settings are intentionally removed from `site_settings.yml`/locales and replaced by the new `embeddable_hosts` table, and the migration attempts to copy the old values into that table before deleting them. So the deletion is intentional cleanup rather than a clear defect, and “risking data loss” is speculative unless rollback support is a hard requirement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost before_validation raises NoMethodError/KeyError when host param is absent or nil

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., missing/blank `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, or any other code path instantiating `EmbeddableHost` without `host`), this will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` before validations can add errors. There is no presence validation to prevent this, and `validates_format_of` does not stop the callback from running.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? behavior change: returns true even with zero configured embeddable hosts

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. While it’s true this can now return true even when there are zero configured embeddable hosts, the host configuration mechanism was moved from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` to the `EmbeddableHost` model/table (and request validation now uses `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`). Given that, removing the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard is not a clear defect; it likely makes truncation depend on whether a topic is actually an embedded topic (`has_topic_embed?`) plus the truncate setting, regardless of current host allowlist state (which may be empty even though existing embedded topics remain).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs only assert subclass ancestry and provide no real coverage of endpoint behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb. Each contains only a single example asserting the controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController, and does not exercise any controller actions (e.g., show/create/update/destroy), responses, authentication/authorization behavior, or serialization. This is directly verifiable in the added spec files and provides essentially no endpoint behavior coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness constraint or validation on embeddable_hosts.host, allowing duplicates with nondeterministic routing

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `EmbeddableHost` model/table with `host` but no `validates :host, uniqueness: ...` and no DB unique index in the migration (`create_table :embeddable_hosts` only adds a plain `t.string :host`). Lookup uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which will return an arbitrary matching row if duplicates exist (no `order`), and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that record’s `category_id`. Therefore duplicate hosts can exist and which one is used can be nondeterministic.
